paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Nehemiah looked at the broken city honestly before he asked anyone to do anything about it. He inspected the wall and the burned gates himself, at night, and told no one what God had laid on his heart (Nehemiah 2:12-16). Then he said the plain truth, "You see the trouble we are in," and offered a plan, "Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem…" (Nehemiah 2:17). He also told them about "the gracious hand of my God upon me," and that's a good way to start a hard job, baker: see it honestly, say it plainly, and point people to what God has already done (Nehemiah 2:18).

Now look at who ended up on that wall. Priests, goldsmiths, perfumers, rulers and whole families each took a section, and Shallum even had his daughters helping (Nehemiah 3:1, 8, 12). Several of them repaired right by their own house, and a few, like Meremoth, took on a second section (Nehemiah 3:10, 28, 4, 21). I LOVE that, friend, because the wall went up one crew at a time, and nobody had to build the whole thing alone. The Tekoites' nobles did not put their shoulders to the work, but the rest kept building (Nehemiah 3:5).

And when the mockers showed up, Nehemiah answered them with God. He said, "The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success," and told them they had "no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem" (Nehemiah 2:20). He trusted God with this rebuilding, and he didn't let the mocking set the pace. So what good work is in front of YOU today, baker? Do your piece with your eyes on God, not on whoever is laughing at you.
